unit_policy.metric_standards: values are transcribed verbatim from the CSV, in millimetres
unit_policy.inch_standards: FreeCAD_FastenersWB stores its ASME tables in MILLIMETRES, not inches (verified per file). Each inch row therefore carries BOTH the verbatim mm value under 'as_published_in_csv_mm' AND an inch value ('*_in') computed as value_mm / 25.4, which is exact by definition of the inch. Nothing was converted silently; both numbers are present.
unit_policy.threads_per_inch: derived as 25.4 / P where P is the CSV pitch column in mm; all derived values land on exact UNC integers (32, 24, 20, 18, 16, 13, 11), which corroborates the derivation
unit_policy.exception_noted: FsData/asmeb18.2.1.1def.csv (UNC SQUARE bolts) IS in inches - per-file unit checking was necessary and was done

_provenance.column_semantics_verified_against_code: Column meanings were not guessed from names. They were confirmed against the workbench's own unpacking of each table: FsFunctions/FSmakeCylinderHeadScrew.py (ISO4762: dk_max=head dia, k=head height, s_mean feeds makeHexRecess so it is the socket A/F, t=socket depth), FsFunctions/FSmakeCountersunkHeadScrew.py (dk_theo/dk_mean/s_mean/t for ISO10642 and ASMEB18.3.2), and ScrewMaker.py GetAllLengths for the length tables. The four socket-screw standards added for the button head and low head lines were read the same way: FsFunctions/FSmakeButtonHeadScrew.py unpacks ISO7380-1 as (P, b, a, da, dk, dk_mean, s_mean, t_min, r, k, e, w) and ASMEB18.3.3A as (P, b, da, dk, s_mean, t_min, r, k), so dk is the head diameter and k the head height in both; FsFunctions/FSmakeCylinderHeadScrew.py unpacks DIN7984 as (P, b, dk_max, da, ds_min, e, k, r, s_mean, t, v, dw) and ASMEB18.3.1G as (P, b, A, H, C_max, J, T, K, r) with dk_max=A, k=H, s_mean=J, t=T.
